steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Modelling builds up form by adding material (clay, plasticine); carving removes material to reveal form (wood, soap, stone).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Casting creates multiples from a mould — plaster, latex, silicone; assemblage joins ready-made or found objects.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sculpture must be considered from ALL viewpoints — walk around it, photograph from multiple angles.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mass (solid volume), volume (enclosed space) and negative space (the spaces within and around) are key 3D concepts.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring 3d form and sculpture techniques. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with 3d form and sculpture techniques. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with 3d form and sculpture techniques. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to 3d form and sculpture techniques, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
